newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Meyer says SFR forex moves still a risk.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Meyer says SFR forex moves still a risk.

text.p: The current trade weighted value of the Swiss franc is at an appropriate level, but exchange rate developments remain a constant risk factor for the Swiss economy, Swiss National Bank president Hans Meyer said.
"The development of the exchange rate remains as a constant risk factor," Meyer said in the text of a speech to business leaders.

"The real trade-weighted Swiss franc is today generally at an appropriate level. Its long-term slightly rising trend does not pose a problem for the economy. Fluctuations around this trend create much more of a problem," he said.
In addition, Meyer said in his speech that creation of a single currency in Europe would at least temporarily pose a danger of a Swiss franc appreciation.

"From the approaching creation of the single currency in Europe there is -- at least temporarily -- a danger of appreciation for the franc," Meyer said. He said such tendencies had led the SNB to be more generous with additions of liquidity in recent days, he said.
"We will remain vigilant and, if necessary, take measures against a development which would endanger the economic recovery," Meyer also said.
The Swiss National Bank has said last Wednesday it was aggressively adding liquidity to the domestic money market to counteract an unwanted rise in the Swiss franc.
